content.text: Ayush Counselling is the centralised counselling process for admission to courses such as Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy, directed under the Ministry of Ayush. The counselling is conducted for both UG and PG courses, and it is mandatory for the aspirants to undergo it after qualifying for the NEET examination.

This article will provide you with everything you need to know about the Ayush Counselling 2025 for UG courses, including their registration fees, important dates, cut-off, and the counseling process. Go through the entire article to learn thoroughly about what is Ayush Counselling and how to participate in the counselling to secure admission to the respective courses.
The registration for Round 1 Ayush Counselling began on August 22nd and is currently ongoing. The last date for registration is September 1, 2025.

sections.heading: Ayush Counselling Overview

content.text: Ayush Counselling for all the courses, BAMS/BSMS/BUMS/BHMS, is conducted by two authorities. Ayush Admissions Central Counselling Committee (AACCC) is the authority conducting counselling for 15% of the All India Quota(AIQ) seats . The remaining 85% of seats are handled by the state counselling authorities . For every institution, the counselling is conducted through their respective state’s responsible authority. The Ayush Counselling process generally involves registration, choice filling, seat allotment, document verification, and reporting to the college.

According to the Ministry of Ayusha and the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), there are 563 BAMS colleges and 57 BUMS colleges across India, Including Private, Government, aided, and deemed colleges. As per the reports of the National Commission of Homeopathy (NCH), 277 colleges in India offer the BHMS course. The BSMS course is offered by 15 colleges in the country.
For participating in the Ayush counselling for the above mentioned courses, it is mandatory to appear and qualify the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) UG examination.
The NEET UG 2025 examination was held on May 4, 2025, and the results were out on 14th June 2025. Ayush Counselling dates are yet to be published by AACCC.

sections.heading: Ayush Counselling 2025- Detailed Process

content.text: AACCC Counselling for UG counselling involves multiple rounds of allotments for maximum seats utilization and and this allows the candidates to upgrade their choices in each round. The procedure starts with the registration and fee payment by the candidates on the official website of AACCC or the concerned state counselling authority. Further, there are choice filling and choice locking, which allow the candidates to choose their preferred colleges. After the processing of allotment, the candidates are required to report to the allotted college for document verification. The allotment takes place in 4 rounds. Each round is explained in detail below.

sections.heading: Types of Ayush Counselling

content.text: The counselling process for Ayush courses is undertaken by two different means. The All India quota seats of 15% are filled through AACCC counseling. The remaining 85% of seats are state quota, for which the concerned State/UT conducts the counselling.

sections.heading: All India Quota (AIQ) seats

content.text: 15% of the seats are under the All India Quota, and the seats are open to all candidates irrespective of their domicile. The candidates from any state and Union Territory can participate in the counselling. It is centralised, national-level counselling regulated by AACCC.

sections.heading: State Quota

content.text: The State Quota reserves 85 % of the seats for candidates who are domicile to a particular State or Union territory. The counselling process is handled by the concerned State authority of the domicile state. Different states possess their respective authorities for counselling across the country. They follow the counselling guidelines and reservation policy of the state government and the counselling conducting authority responsible. sections.heading: What is the registration fee for Ayush counselling?

content.text: Ayush Counselling cutoff 2025 for NEET is yet to be announced. The cutoff percentiles are 50th, 40th, 40th, 40th for UR/EWS, OBC, SC, ST, respectively.

sections.heading: Who is eligible for Ayush Counselling 2025?

content.text: The candidates who qualified the NEET UG examination and have 10+2 from a recognized board with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/ Biotechnology as core subjects are eligible to participate in Ayush Counselling 2025.

sections.heading: What is the Ayush Cutoff 2025 for the SC/ST category?

content.text: The Ayush Cutoff Score for 2025 SC/ST category is 143-113, and 40th percentile. For candidates belonging to SC/ST (PwD category), the cutoff score is 126-113.

Ayush Counselling registration fees for Govt/ Govt.Aided/ National Institute /Central University are INR 1000/- and INR 500/- for UR/EWS/OBC-NCL and PwBD categories, respectively. In case of Deemed University, it is INR 5000/- for all categories.

What is the Ayush counselling cutoff 2025 for NEET?

Ayush Counselling cutoff 2025 for NEET is yet to be announced. The cutoff percentiles are 50th, 40th, 40th, 40th for UR/EWS, OBC, SC, ST, respectively.

Who is eligible for Ayush Counselling 2025?

The candidates who qualified the NEET UG examination and have 10+2 from a recognized board with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/ Biotechnology as core subjects are eligible to participate in Ayush Counselling 2025.

What is the Ayush Cutoff 2025 for the SC/ST category?

The Ayush Cutoff Score for 2025 SC/ST category is 143-113, and 40th percentile. For candidates belonging to SC/ST (PwD category), the cutoff score is 126-113.
